rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For numerals three through ten, the counted noun normally takes a paucity plural; since aqraʾ exists, the use of the abundance plural qurūʾ needs explanation.
rows.anchor: جمع كثرة، ومن ثلاثة إلى عشرة يميز بجموع القلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation counts all the divorced women together: each waits three periods, making the aggregate number of periods large.
rows.anchor: لما جمع المطلقات جمع القروء، لأن كل مطلقة تتربص ثلاثة أقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation allows one plural pattern to stand broadly in place of the other.
rows.anchor: أنه من باب الاتساع ووضع أحد الجمعين موضع الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation derives qurūʾ from qarʾ with fatḥa; aqraʾ would be irregular because afʿāl is not a regular plural for this faʿl pattern.
rows.anchor: الثالث: أن قروءا جمع قرء بفتح القاف، فلو جاء على " أقراء " لجاء على غير القياس

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad estimates “three of periods,” with min omitted; Abu al-Baqāʾ's expanded estimate is the same analysis.
rows.anchor: والرابع - وهو مذهب المبرد -:أن التقدير " ثلاثة من قروء " ، فحذف " من "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed root sense is a recurring appointed time: the star's qarʾ is its rising or setting, and aqraʾa al-najm means it rose or set.
rows.anchor: أصله الوقت المعتاد تردده، ومنه: قرء النجم لوقت طلوعه وأفوله

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses qāriʾ for the appointed time when winds blow, supporting the time sense.
rows.anchor: شنئت العقر عقر بني شليل إذا هبت لقارئها الرياح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed origins are transition from purity to menstruation or the reverse, and gathering; the gathering-water etymology is rejected because that verb has a weak y-root while qarʾ is hamzated.
rows.anchor: أصله الخروج من طهر إلى حيض أو عكسه، وقيل: هو من قولهم: قريت الماء في الحوض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Linguists disagree whether menstruation and purity are homonyms or share an underlying common meaning such as gathering, time, or transition.
rows.anchor: وإذا تقرر ما ذكرت لك فاعلم أن أهل العلم اختلفوا في إطلاقه على الحيض والطهر

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: A woman’s qarʾ can denote her time of menstruation or purity; al-Akhfash distinguishes aqraʾat, becoming menstruating, from qaraʾat, menstruating.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: أقرأت أي: صارت ذات حيض، وقرأت بغير ألف أي: حاضت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other definitions are menstruation together with purity, or the interval between two menstruations.
rows.anchor: وقيل: القرء: الحيض مع الطهر، وقيل: ما بين الحيضتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarʾ may originally mean gathering, as in gathering water in a basin and reciting the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أصله الجمع، ومنه: قرأت الماء في الحوض: جمعته، ومنه: قرأ القرآن

rows.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
rows.claim: Ibn Kulthūm's verse uses taqraʾ for gathering a fetus; on the gathering derivation, menstruation gathers blood in the womb and purity gathers blood in the body.
rows.anchor: ذراعي عيطل أدماء بكر هجان اللون لم تقرأ جنينا

rows.speaker: جمهور أهل اللسان
rows.claim: Most linguists, including Abū ʿAmr, Yūnus, and Abū ʿUbayda, take menstruation and purity as homonyms/opposites rather than senses sharing one meaning.
rows.anchor: ولكن القائل بالاشتراك اللفظي وجعلهما من الأضداد هم جمهور أهل اللسان كأبي عمرو ويونس وأبي عبيدة

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā uses qurūʾ for periods of purity, as the context refers to the loss of the women's pure intervals.
rows.anchor: قول الأعشى: 973 أفي كل عام أنت جاشم غزوة

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses qurūʾ for menstruation, likening a man's flowing blood to a menstruating woman's blood.
rows.anchor: قوله: 974 يا رب ذي ضغن علي فارض له قروء

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī transmits qarʾ with ḍamma, while Abū Zayd transmits it with fatḥa; both forms mean the same.
rows.anchor: ويقال " قرء " بالضم نقله الأصمعي، و " قرء " بالفتح نقله أبو زيد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads thalāthata qarū, with fatḥa on qāf, silent rāʾ, light wāw, and no hamza; he treats the number as annexed to a generic noun and uses a dialect form of qarʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: " ثلاثة قرو " بفتح القاف وسكون الراء وتخفيف الواو من غير همز

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī, also reported from Nāfiʿ, reads qurūww with doubled wāw, easing the hamza to wāw and assimilating the preceding wāw.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري - ويروى عن نافع -: " قرو " بتشديد الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in lahunna is attached to yaḥillu and is the lām of communication, as in “I said to you.”
rows.anchor: قوله: { لهن } متعلق ب " يحل، واللام للتبليغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stronger parsing makes mā a relative pronoun meaning “that which”; its resumptive pronoun is omitted, estimated mā khalaqahu.
rows.anchor: قوله: { ما خلق } في " ما " وجهان، أظهرهما: أنها موصولة بمعنى الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, mā is an indefinite noun described by the following clause; like the relative analysis, it has an omitted resumptive pronoun.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنها نكرة موصوفة، وعلى كلا التقديرين فالعائد محذوف لاستكمال الشروط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā may refer to the fetus, treated grammatically as nonrational, or to menstrual blood.
rows.anchor: و " ما " يجوز أن يراد بها الجنين وهو في حكم غير العاقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī arḥāmihinna can attach directly to khalaqa, or modify the omitted resumptive pronoun circumstantially: what God created, existing in their wombs.
rows.anchor: قوله: { في أرحامهن } فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أن يتعلق بخلق. والثاني: أن يتعلق بمحذوف

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ calls the circumstantial reading prospective, since at the time of creation the fetus is not yet a thing until its creation is complete.
rows.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " لأن وقت خلقه ليس بشيء حتى يتم خلقه "

rows.speaker: مبشر بن عبيد
rows.claim: Mubashshir ibn ʿUbayd reads both hāʾ pronouns with ḍamma, the original form and a Hijazi usage; kasra harmonizes with a preceding yāʾ or kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مبشر بن عبيد: " في أرحامهن " و " بردهن " بضم هاء الكناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional's answer may be omitted and recovered from the preceding prohibition: if they believe, they must not conceal.
rows.anchor: قوله: { إن كن } هذا شرط، وفي جوابه المذهبان المشهوران: إما محذوف، وتقديره من لفظ ما تقدم

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans and Abū Zayd allow the answer to precede the conditional, with the earlier prohibition serving as its answer.
rows.anchor: وإما أنه متقدم كما هو مذهب الكوفيين وأبي زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking in as meaning idh, “when,” is a weak analysis.
rows.anchor: وقيل: " إن " بمعنى إذ وهو ضعيف.

rows.speaker: مسلمة بن محارب
rows.claim: The majority pronounce the tāʾ of baʿūlatuhunna with fatḥa; Muslimah ibn Muḥārib silences it to avoid consecutive vowel movements, as in a reading of 43:30.
rows.anchor: الجمهور على رفع تاء بعولتهن، وسكنها مسلمة بن محارب، وذلك لتوالي الحركات فخفف، ونظيره قراءة:

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abū Zayd reports silencing the nominative ending in rusulunā; Abū ʿAmr reports that Tamīm similarly silences nominatives such as yaʿlamuhum.
rows.anchor: ورسلنا لديهم يكتبون [الزخرف: 30] بسكون اللام حكاها أبو زيد، وحكى أبو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥaqqu is the predicate of baʿūlatuhunna and means “entitled,” not comparative: outsiders have no claim, and a wife's refusal does not invalidate a husband's revocation.
rows.anchor: و " أحق " خبر عن " بعولتهن " وهو بمعنى حقيقون، إذ لا معنى للتفضيل هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿūla is the plural of baʿl, husband; its tāʾ marks a feminine collective plural like fuhūla and dhukūra, a pattern that is not productive.
rows.anchor: والبعولة: جمع " بعل " وهو زوج المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿūla is also a verbal noun of baʿala; ḥasanat al-tabāʿul describes a good wife, while bāʿalahā is a euphemism for intercourse.
rows.anchor: والبعولة أيضا مصدر بعل الرجل بعولة وبعالا، وامرأة حسنة التبعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-raddihinna is attached to aḥaqqu.
rows.anchor: قوله: { بردهن } متعلق بأحق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If fī dhālika attaches to aḥaqqu, dhālika means the waiting period: the husband has the right to revoke during it, restoring her to the marriage.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنه متعلق أيضا بأحق، ويكون المشار إليه بذلك على هذا العدة

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Alternatively, fī dhālika attaches to the act of revocation, and dhālika refers to marriage.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن تتعلق بالرد ويكون المشار إليه بذلك على هذا النكاح، قاله أبو البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in baʿūlatuhunna refers to some divorced women, specifically those whose divorces are revocable.
rows.anchor: والضمير في " بعولتهن " عائد على بعض المطلقات وهن الرجعيات خاصة

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh prefers an understood annexed noun, “husbands of their revocably divorced women,” which makes the pronoun refer to all divorced women.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " والأولى عندي أن يكون على حذف مضاف دل عليه الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause has a fronted predicate; its balanced ellipsis removes “against their husbands” where “against them” appears, and “for their husbands” where “for them” appears.
rows.anchor: وأصل التركيب. ولهن على أزواجهن مثل الذي لأزواجهن عليهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-l-maʿrūf can attach to the predicate governing lahunna, meaning their due is established according to recognized practice.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن يتعلق بما تعلق به " لهن " من الاستقرار أي: استقر لهن بالمعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it modifies mithl as a deleted adjective; because mithl does not become definite through annexation, the phrase is nominative in this parse rather than accusative in the first.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنه صفة لمثل، لأن " مثل " لا يتعرف بالإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stronger parse makes li-l-rijāli a fronted predicate and darajatun the delayed subject; ʿalayhinna either attaches to that predicate or is a fronted circumstantial modifier of daraja.
rows.anchor: أظهرهما: أن " للرجال " خبر مقدم و " درجة " مبتدأ مؤخر

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows ʿalayhinna as predicate and li-l-rijāli as a circumstantial modifier, arguing that preposing a prepositional phrase before a semantic governor can be strong.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون " عليهن " هو الخبر، و " للرجال " حال من " درجة "

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh rejects this parse outright: the circumstantial precedes both sentence constituents, unlike the disputed intermediate order; Abū al-Ḥasan allows the latter, while others forbid it.
rows.anchor: قال: " فأبو الحسن يجيزها وغيره يمنعها "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farijālan is a circumstantial accusative with an omitted governor: either “pray walking” or, preferably, “maintain the prayer walking.”
rows.anchor: منصوب على الحال، والعامل فيه محذوف تقديره: " فصلوا رجالا، أو فحافظوا عليها رجالا وهذا أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijāl is a plural of rāʾil/rājil, a person walking on foot without a mount; the cited verse and poetry attest this sense.
rows.anchor: و " رجال " جمع راجل كقائم وقيام، وصاحب وصحاب، يقال منه: رجل يرجل رجلا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses rajulān for walking barefoot to the House of God, witnessing the word's on-foot sense.
rows.anchor: علي إذا لاقيت ليلى بخفية أن أزدار بيت الله رجلان حافيا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Many dialect plurals are listed for the walking person; forms include rajāli, rajāla, rajalān, rajla, arjila, arājil, and arājīl, with readings attributed to ʿIkrima and Ibn Mukhallad and a rare rajjulan.
rows.anchor: وتروى قراءة عن عكرمة، ورجالى ورجالة ورجال وبها قرأ عكرمة وابن مخلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾanic parallel in 22:27 and another poem use rijālan for going on foot beneath riding animals.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى: يأتوك رجالا وعلى كل ضامر [الحج: 27]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rukbān is the plural of rākib; some reserve it for camel riders, calling a horse rider fāris and a donkey or mule rider by the animal's name, though ṣāḥib is better.
rows.anchor: وركبان جمع راكب، قيل: ولا يقال إلا لمن ركب جملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction aw is variously read as division between cases, permission, or a choice between alternatives.
rows.anchor: و " أو " هنا للتقسيم وقيل: للإباحة، وقيل: للتخيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf is accusative as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun or a circumstantial of its pronoun; it may instead express cause: remember God because He taught you.
rows.anchor: الكاف في محل نصب: إما نعتا لمصدر محذوف، أو حالا من ضمير المصدر المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is most naturally a verbal noun; alternatively it is relative, making the command “pray like the prayer He taught you,” with remembrance standing for prayer and the comparison between prayer in danger and safety.
rows.anchor: و " ما " يجوز أن تكون مصدرية وهو الظاهر، ويجوز أن تكون بمعنى الذي

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya parses mā lam takūnū as a substitute for the mā in kamā; the Shaykh accepts this but prefers it as substitute for the omitted resumptive pronoun in ʿallamakum, with an Arabic example supporting that ellipsis.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: " وعلى هذا التأويل يكون قوله: { ما لم تكونوا } بدلا من " ما " في " كما "

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh prefers taking mā lam takūnū as a substitute for the omitted pronoun in ʿallamakum (allamakumūhu), a construction grammarians permit.
rows.anchor: وأحسن منه أن يكون " ما لم تكونوا " بدلا من الضمير المحذوف في " علمكم " العائد على الموصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wusʿahā is the second object of yukallifu. Ibn ʿAṭiyya says another object is omitted, but the Shaykh says that is true only at the verb's underlying valency, not in the surface syntax.
rows.anchor: " وسعها " مفعول ثان. وقال ابن عطية: " يكلف " يتعدى إلى مفعولين

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh rejects an omitted object in the grammatical parse: wusʿahā itself is the second object, like dirhaman after an exceptive in “I gave Zayd only a dirham.”
rows.anchor: بل الثاني هو " وسعها " نحو: وما أعطيت زيدا إلا درهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wusʿ is what a person can contain or bear without constriction or exceeding capacity.
rows.anchor: والوسع: ما يسع الإنسان، ولا يضيق عليه، ولا يخرج منه.

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAblah reads the phrase as the past verb wasiʿahā; one parse supplies a deleted relative mā, making it the second object, a construction Basrans reject and Kufans allow, though the omission is weak.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة: " إلا وسعها " جعله فعلا ماضيا، وخرجوا هذه القراءة على أن الفعل

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Another parse of Ibn Abī ʿAblah's reading deletes the second object for clarity and makes the clause an adjective of it; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the reading permissible through inversion, comparing 2:255 and 20:98.
rows.anchor: وقد خرجت هذه القراءة على وجه آخر: وهو أن تجعل المفعول الثاني محذوفا لفهم المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence has no syntactic position, since it gives information; another analysis makes it an accusative supplement to “we hear and obey,” meaning they also said this.
rows.anchor: الظاهر الثاني لأنها سيقت للإخبار بذلك، وقيل: بل محلها نصب عطفا على " سمعنا "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lahā mā kasabat is an independent explanatory sentence: being answerable only for one's own deeds illustrates that God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.
rows.anchor: هذه الجملة لا محل لها لاستئنافها وهي كالتفسير لما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some distinguish the verbs: kasaba can mean earning for oneself or another, whereas iktasaba is narrower; Arabic says “he earns for his family” but not “he acquires his family,” and al-Ḥuṭayʾa's line uses kāsib.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم: نعم، وفرق بأن الكسب أعم، إذ يقال: " كسب " لنفسه ولغيره

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says evil takes the intensive iktasaba because the desirous self exerts effort to reach it, while good is described by the unmarked kasaba because it follows the path.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " فإن قلت: لم خص الخير بالكسب والشر بالاكتساب؟ قلت: في الاكتساب اعتمال

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya first suggests the different forms simply vary the wording elegantly, as in 86:17; the author instead sees a semantic distinction in the effort involved in good and evil.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " وكرر فعل الكسب فخالف بين التصريف حسنا لنمط الكلام، كما قال تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers a distinction: good is earned without strain along God's prescribed way, while sin requires the intensified effort of breaking His prohibition.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر لي في هذا أن الحسنات هي مما يكسب دون تكلف، إذ كاسبها على جادة أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others find no difference, noting that the Qurʾān uses both forms for evil: 74:38, 6:164, and 33:58.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: " لا فرق، وقد جاء القرآن بالكسب والاكتساب في مورد واحد

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ reports both the view that the forms are synonymous and the view that iftaʿala signals effort, making sin weighty in its consequences.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " وقال قوم: " لا فرق بينهما، وذكر نحوا مما تقدم. وقال آخرون: " افتعل يدل على شدة الكلفة

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says the sound linguistic view treats kasb and iktisāb as equivalent, citing Dhū al-Rummah's line that uses both forms together.
rows.anchor: وقال الواحدي: " الصحيح عند أهل اللغة أن الكسب والاكتساب واحد لا فرق بينهما، قال ذو الرمة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tuʾākhidhnā is read with hamza from taking someone to task; the wāw reading either eases hamza to wāw by regular phonology or derives from wākhadhahu, as Abū al-Baqāʾ says.
rows.anchor: يقرأ بالهمزة وهو من الأخذ بالذنب، ويقرأ بالواو، ويحتمل وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciprocal form is used for one action because the sinner exposes himself to punishment by his deed, as if helping the punisher act against him; it may also be a conventional reciprocal such as sāfartu.
rows.anchor: وجاء هنا بلفظ المفاعلة وهو فعل واحد، لأن المسيء قد أمكن من نفسه

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy reads rabbanā wa-lā tuḥammil ʿalaynā iṣran with a doubled mīm; al-Zamakhsharī explains this as intensifying “lay a burden upon.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي: " ربنا ولا تحمل علينا إصرا " بتشديد الميم

words: وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī distinguishes the two doubled forms: the first intensifies carrying upon someone, while the second causatively shifts ḥamala from one object to two.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " فإن قلت: أي فرق بين هذه الشديدة والتي في " ولا تحملنا؟ قلت: هذه للمبالغة

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Iṣr fundamentally means weight or severity; al-Nābigha's verse calls it a burden borne after the people have been exhausted.
rows.anchor: والإصر: في الأصل الثقل والشدة. وقال النابغة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a covenant is heavy, iṣr also means covenant or compact, as in God's covenant taken from the prophets in 3:81.
rows.anchor: وأطلق على العهد والميثاق لثقلهما، كقوله تعالى: وأخذتم على ذلكم إصري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in lahā conveys ownership and the pleasure of good; ʿalā in ʿalayhā conveys evil's burden weighing upon its bearer.
rows.anchor: اللام تقتضي الملك والخير يحب ويسر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says even a slight good is credited graciously by God, while punishment follows only deliberate striving; the author says this depends on distinguishing the verb forms and finds that distinction strongest.
rows.anchor: أدنى فعل من أفعال الخير يكون للإنسان تكرما من الله على عبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iṣr in 7:157 means burdensome legal duties; it broadens to anything heavy, and some reportedly interpret it here as enemies' gloating, citing an unnamed poet.
rows.anchor: ويضع عنهم إصرهم [الأعراف: 157] أي: التكاليف الشاقة ثم يطلق على كل ما يثقل

rows.speaker: الحطيئة
rows.claim: Iṣr can also mean affection or kinship; al-Ḥuṭayʾa says that no tie of kinship draws him to the person.
rows.anchor: ويقال: الإصر أيضا: العطف والقرابة، يقال: " ما يأصرني عليه آصرة " أي: ما يعطفني عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iṣr may be the thing by which objects are bound; iṣār is the cord securing loads, from the verb aṣara, “to bind.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: الإصر: الأمر الذي تربط به الأشياء، ومنه " الإصار " للحبل الذي تشد به الأحمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun iṣr is also transmitted with ḍamma on its hamza in a rare reading.
rows.anchor: ويقال بضمها أيضا، وقد قرىء به شاذا

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy's doubled mīm in lā tuḥammil ʿalaynā intensifies the action.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي: { ولا تحمل علينآ } بالتشديد مبالغة في الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭāqa means ability and is an irregularly shortened verbal noun of aṭāqa; the expected form is iṭāqa, like other exceptional maṣdars such as ghāra, jāba, and nabāt, and it is not productive.
rows.anchor: والطاقة: القدرة على الشيء وهي في الأصل، مصدر، جاءت على حذف الزوائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author supports the exceptional verbal-noun pattern with Qurʾān 71:17 and a poetic example of ʿaṭāʾ.
rows.anchor: ونظير أجاب جابة: أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا [نوح: 17] وأعطى عطاء في قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawlā is a mafʿal from wali/yali; here it is a verbal noun used for an agent, possibly with an omitted “possessor of our guardianship,” and it may also denote place or time.
rows.anchor: والمولى: مفعل من ولي يلي، وهو هنا مصدر يراد به الفاعل، فيجوز أن يكون على حذف مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ marks causation: because God is their protector and manages their affairs, they ask Him to grant victory over their enemies.
rows.anchor: أتى هنا بالفاء إعلاما بالسببية؛ لأن الله تعالى لما كان مولاهم ومالك أمورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author illustrates this causal appeal with “You are generous, so grant me” and “You are a hero, so protect your sanctuary.”
rows.anchor: كقولك " أنت الجواد فتكرم علي وأنت البطل فاحم حرمك "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra contains many branches of learning; most have already been indicated, and an intelligent reader can infer what is suggested without explicit detail.
rows.anchor: وقد اشتملت هذه السورة على أنواع كثيرة من العلوم، تقدم التبيه على غالبها

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: One parse supplies an omitted udhkur: idh is then a direct object, not a time adverb; Abū al-Ḥasan and Abū al-ʿAbbās hold this view.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أنه " اذكر " مقدرا، فيكون مفعولا به لا ظرفا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Another parse supplies an understood iṣṭafā from the earlier verb and attaches idh to it; this makes “the family of ʿImrān” a clause-level coordination, avoiding the impossible claim that Adam's choosing coincided with the wife's speech.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أن الناصب له معنى الاصطفاء أي ب " اصطفى " مقدرا مدلولا عليه باصطفى الأول

rows.speaker: ابن جرير الطبري
rows.claim: Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī explicitly makes idh depend on samīʿ; al-Zamakhsharī appears to do likewise, for hearing her speech and intention.
rows.anchor: الثالث: أنه منصوب ب " سميع " وبه صرح ابن جرير الطبري

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh rejects attachment to samīʿ: ʿalīm either interrupts the government or qualifies samīʿ before it takes its object, and divine hearing and knowledge are not time-limited; the author replies that adverbials allow such flexibility.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ولا يصح ذلك لأن قوله " عليم ": إما أن يكون خبرا بعد خبر

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats idh as redundant; grammarians call this an error, and the author says Abū ʿUbayda was weak in grammar.
rows.anchor: الرابع: أن تكون " إذ " زائدة وهو قول أبي عبيدة، والتقدير: قالت امرأة، وهذا عند النحويين غلط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥarraran may be a circumstantial from the relative phrase mā fī baṭnī, governed by nadhartu.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أنه حال من الموصول وهو " ما في بطني " ، فالعامل فيها " نذرت "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is circumstantial from the pronoun governed by the preposition in mā fī baṭnī, with the implicit existential of that phrase as its governor.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أنه حال من الضمير المرفوع بالجار لوقوعه صلة ل " ما " ، وهو قريب من الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥarraran can be a verbal noun on the passive-participle pattern: either with an omitted “vow of emancipation” or by sense, since nadhartu laka means “I freed as a freeing.”
rows.anchor: الثالث: أن ينتصب على المصدر؛ لأن المصدر يأتي على زنة اسم المفعول من الفعل الزائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pattern is illustrated by Qurʾān 34:19 and 22:18 and a poet's masraḥ al-qawāfī, meaning tasrīḥ al-qawāfī.
rows.anchor: ومن مجيء المصدر بزنة المفعول مما زاد على الثلاثي قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: مكي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Makkī makes muḥarraran an adjective of a deleted object, “a freed boy”; Ibn ʿAṭiyya questions this because nadhara already has mā fī baṭnī as its object.
rows.anchor: الرابع: أن يكون نعت مفعول محذوف تقديره: غلاما محررا، قاله مكي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If muḥarraran is circumstantial, it is contemporaneous when it means emancipation, but prospective when it means service in a church, as reported in tafsīr.
rows.anchor: وعلى القول بأنها حال يجوز أن تكون حالا مقارنة إن أريد بالتحرير معنى العتق

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī pause on imraʾah with hāʾ despite the written tāʾ; Medinans pause with tāʾ following the muṣḥaf spelling, an Arabic dialect also heard in ḥamzat and witnessed by a poet's Muslimat.
rows.anchor: ووقف أبو عمرو والكسائي على " امرأة " بالهاء دون التاء، وقد كتبوا امرأة بالتاء

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة
rows.claim: The people of Medina pause with tāʾ according to the written muṣḥaf; comparable pause forms occur in “the wife of al-ʿAzīz,” Noah's and Lot's wives, and Pharaoh's wife.
rows.anchor: وأهل المدينة يقفون بالتاء اتباعا لرسم المصحف، وهي لغة للعرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is used instead of man because the contents of the womb are still unknown; those restricting mā to nonrational referents explain it by that ambiguity or the fetus's lack of discernment, while those allowing rational referents need no special explanation.
rows.anchor: وقوله: { ما في بطني } أتى ب " ما " التي لغير العاقل لأن ما فيه بطنها مبهم أمره
